title: A REGISTER -- rows a host keeps about one subject, each in a status its kind declares
description: ADR-022 decision 10, amendment 3. Findings, visions, the standards met, the questions the doctrine could not answer: each is a register of ROWS, and a row's status is a word its KIND declares -- with what that status requires the row to carry. A row is never deleted; it is re-statused, so the history of an understanding survives, and git dates every change. A row PROMOTED out of a register names where it went, and that place cites the row back (`<register>#<row>`): a promotion recorded at one end only is how a rule acquires clauses nobody can date.

kind.description: The register kind whose statuses this register's rows are in.

at.description: When the row took its present status.

declared_at.description: The ONE place the subject is declared -- `—` would be the finding itself, so a row with no home leaves this out.

promoted_to.description: Where this row went, a path that cites it back.
